mode: correction, supersedes the earlier 2026-09-01 board (pre-Week 1, rosters full, FAAB market not yet open)
note: CORRECTION. The first 2026-09-01 pass ranked Tre Tucker as the #1 PURSUE on beat-reporter role narrative and never checked the projection against the rest of the pool. Re-scoring Sleeper's live 2026 projections into HBGBs settings puts Tucker at 102.9, BELOW Kayshon Boutte (104.7), the player he was supposed to replace, and 11th among free-agent WRs behind Meyers (137.4), Coker (136.0), Shakir (135.0), Shaheed (116.0) and even his own teammate Jalen Nailor (108.0). The role news is real (he holds the RWR1 depth slot) but it is already priced in: Sleeper projects 46/582/3, worse than his own 2025 line, because Brock Bowers is the offense's alpha and the quarterback is rookie Fernando Mendoza. Tucker is re-ranked AVOID and the WRs the first pass missed are ranked above him. Sleeper reports season_type regular / week 1, but no NFL games have been played (openers Sept 10-13) and every roster's waiver_budget_used is still 0; all six week-1 league transactions processed as free_agent claims with empty waiver_budget, so a claim made now is a straight free-agent add at zero cost, not a contested bid. rate_basis is preseason projection throughout, not in-season trend.

targets.why: Clear WR2 in Carolina opposite Tetairoa McMillan, backed by a three-year, 34-million-dollar extension signed in July 2026 and camp reports praising his route running and conditioning (Yahoo Sports, Pro Football Network, Fantasy Guru, all Aug 2026). Finished 2025 second on the team in receiving yards, 33-394-3 in 11 games.
targets.asset: 136.0 projected points in HBGBs scoring, the best combination of role certainty and health in the free-agent WR pool. Sleeper depth chart lists him SWR2 with no injury designation.
targets.my_team_impact: Doesn't crack my starting ten over Pickens (206) / Egbuka (186) / Odunze (174), but he is a genuine upgrade on the WR6 spot: +31 over Boutte for the same roster slot, and real cover for the Week 10 bye that takes Egbuka, Odunze, Irving and the Eagles DEF off the field at once.
targets.worth: FAAB 4-6 ceiling as a bench stash if the market were open. The marginal upgrade over Boutte, decayed by nothing this early in the calendar.
targets.confidence_why: Role, contract and health are all cleanly reported, but there are zero 2026 regular-season snaps behind any of it, which caps confidence below high no matter how clean the report reads.
targets.competition: mfkr (WR 368, 9th, -236 vs median) and Sladsous (WR 365, 10th, -238) both carry real WR holes, and mfkr already made a week-1 free-agent add, so he is transacting right now. With claims free until FAAB opens, the pressure is on claiming first rather than on price.
targets.bid: Free-agent claim, FAAB waivers haven't opened
targets.drop: Kayshon Boutte (HOU), 104.7, role reads in_flux, 13.6 expected games. The only genuinely dead spot on my bench.

targets.why: Two straight top-40 finishes, WR36 in 2025 on 72-719-4, now bumped to WR2 in Buffalo by DJ Moore's arrival, which is why he is available rather than why he is bad (Yahoo Sports, Pro Football Network, Aug 2026).
targets.asset: 135.0 projected points and the longest production track record in this group. Sleeper lists him SWR2, Questionable with an undisclosed issue.
targets.my_team_impact: Same slot logic as Coker: +30 on Boutte, bench depth and Week 10 bye cover, no path into my starting ten as currently built.
targets.worth: FAAB 4-6 ceiling. The track record is worth as much here as the projection is.
targets.confidence_why: The production history is the most established in the pool, but the Questionable tag is undisclosed and the DJ Moore signing is a real target-share threat, so the role is genuinely reduced and not just cheap.
targets.competition: The same WR-needy pair, mfkr and Sladsous. Sladsous is tagged dead on trades but does work the wire; mfkr is an early-burner already transacting.
targets.bid: Free-agent claim, FAAB waivers haven't opened
targets.drop: Kayshon Boutte (HOU), same reasoning. Only one of these WRs should be claimed: the bench has one dead spot, not two.

targets.why: Led Jacksonville in target share after arriving in Week 10 of 2025 and signed a three-year extension to stay, putting him in contention for the team target lead. But he is competing with Brian Thomas Jr., Parker Washington, Travis Hunter and Brenton Strange in one of the hardest receiver rooms in the league to forecast (CBS Sports, Sports Illustrated, Yahoo Sports, Aug 2026).
targets.asset: 137.4 projected points, the highest in the free-agent WR pool. Against that, Sleeper's own depth chart lists him RWR3 and he carries a Questionable tag with a hand injury.
targets.my_team_impact: Highest raw number of the three, so on projection alone he is the pick. The depth-chart placement and the hand are why he ranks third instead. Same bench slot, same Boutte drop.
targets.worth: FAAB 3-5 ceiling, discounted off the raw projection for the target competition.
targets.confidence_why: The projection and the depth chart contradict each other (RWR3 versus team target leader), and a hand injury on a possession receiver is not nothing. Two conflicting signals cap this at low until Week 1 settles which one is right.
targets.competition: No rival is chasing a crowded-room WR3 this early, and the name has not surfaced in this league's free-agent traffic.
targets.bid: Free-agent claim, FAAB waivers haven't opened
targets.drop: n/a, watch and revisit once Week 1 clarifies the Jacksonville pecking order.

targets.why: RE-RANKED FROM PURSUE TO AVOID. The Raiders' new staff under Klint Kubiak does have him in the WR1 depth slot (Sleeper lists him RWR1) and he led the team in targets in 2025. But Sleeper's own 2026 projection prices that role at 46-582-3, worse than his 2025 line of 57-696-5, because Brock Bowers is the offense's alpha and the quarterback is rookie Fernando Mendoza. Beat coverage of the depth chart is titled 'No Clear No. 1 Option' and Las Vegas waited until pick 195 to address receiver in the draft (Yahoo Sports / Sportsnaut, Aug 2026).
targets.asset: 102.9 projected points, below Kayshon Boutte (104.7), the bench player he would replace, and below his own teammate Jalen Nailor (108.0). Half-PPR ADP of 181.6 confirms the market reads him as a late dart, not a breakout.
targets.my_team_impact: NEGATIVE. Adding him for Boutte is 104.7 to 102.9, a lateral-to-worse swap that also burns the only dead spot on my bench, which should go to a 135-point WR instead. The national add wave (50,592 adds, 9th on Sleeper's trending list) is chasing a headline the projection has already absorbed.
targets.worth: Zero to my roster specifically. He is the 11th-best free-agent WR by projection.
targets.confidence_why: This is not a role dispute. The projection already grants him the WR1 role and still lands below my worst bench WR, and three independent signals agree (projection, ADP, depth-chart reporting), so the avoid holds even preseason.
targets.competition: Heavy national add volume, no sign of interest inside this league. Letting him go costs nothing.

targets.why: Listed RWR2 in Seattle with no injury designation, projecting 116.0 in HBGBs scoring. A healthy body in a defined role, which is more than most of this pool offers.
targets.asset: Field-stretcher profile: spike weeks on deep shots, thin floor between them. In half PPR at 0.5 per reception, the low-catch weeks hurt more than the yardage helps.
targets.my_team_impact: Marginal. +11 on Boutte, not enough to justify a claim when Coker and Shakir sit there at +30.
targets.confidence_why: Role and health are both clean. The cap is that a boom-bust shape is a poor fit for a bench spot whose whole job is covering a bye week predictably.
targets.bid: Free-agent claim, FAAB waivers haven't opened

targets.why: Signed by Carolina Aug 12 as the presumptive top pass-catching TE over Ja'Tavion Sanders and Tommy Tremble (NBC Sports, CBS Sports). Unchanged from the earlier board.
targets.asset: 99.0 projected points. Veteran red-zone target in a run-funnel offense, but Bryce Young has thrown only 49 TD passes in 44 career starts, a TD-dependent profile with a low weekly floor.
targets.my_team_impact: None. I carry LaPorta (159) and Ferguson (125), and Ferguson is real insurance given LaPorta is Questionable with a hip and a herniated-disc history behind him. That TE2 spot is not available.
targets.worth: Low-end TE2 streamer value league-wide, nothing to my roster.
targets.confidence_why: The role is reported clearly; the ceiling is capped by a low-volume-TD quarterback. The confidence is about the modest outlook, not the role.
targets.competition: Stipe owns the league's worst TE room (Goedert 110, 10th, -41 vs median) and is the one owner with a real reason to move here.
